title: Response goal card on UnlockPickup: 9 of 9 learned
subtitle: The Response goal card (`tpl-response-1-goal`) moved from KeyCorridorS6R3, where no method solved it, to UnlockPickup. Its three accepted machines trained on 3 seeds each and all 9 runs learned.

blocks.title: In plain words
blocks.text: The card says: whenever you hold the key, the door must be open then or later; pick up the key, open the door, then pick up the box in the other room. On UnlockPickup, every machine the card accepts (the expected answer and its two accepted alternatives) trained to a policy that passes the judge on every seed: 100 of 100 greedy test episodes hold every hard rule and reach the goal. The three machines pay 13, 12 and 12 for the finish, and finish in 17 to 18 steps.

items: **Setup.** One-hot machine state, PPO setting s07 (16 envs x 256 steps, lr 1e-3), 1.5M steps, procedural layouts, seeds 1 to 3 per machine. Judge: 100 greedy test episodes per run (test seeds from 2000000); a seed learned when the hard rules held in at least 0.8 of them.

**Gate before training.** Each machine passed the pay-order check, the bundle review, a plan-trace check (75 traces, 0 mismatches) and the labeling check against the reference (5,047 compared, 0 differ). No model call, no change to the compiler.
**Scripted baselines on the same seeds.** Idle: hard rules held 0.00, length 288. The solving plan: 1.00, length 19.

blocks.text: On the old environment, `MiniGrid-KeyCorridorS6R3-v0`, no method solved this card. The card's old machine (solve pay 21:1, 43:1, 51:11) trained 0 of 3. A sweep of every run folder in the main checkout and 24 worktrees found 0 of 71 KeyCorridorS6R3 runs that learned, and no run on a smaller KeyCorridor size. The project rule is that an unsolved card moves to a level that is learnable, instead of retrying the same one.

UnlockPickup has the same chain (key, locked door, box in another room), is the easier version, and had learned runs: ARM-FM 3 of 3 and FARM 1 of 3 (below), and 4 of 27 runs in the whole sweep (DoorKey-8x8: 45 of 72; BlockedUnlockPickup: 22 of 178). It was also the one level with a learned run and no Response goal card, so the three Response goal cards now sit on three levels (DoorKey, BlockedUnlockPickup, UnlockPickup). The new wording keeps the Response sentence of the other two cards and adds the chain. Card change: commit `0e821b8`, merged as `54f2c71`.

sections.title: The three machines
sections.intro: Each graph is the live RM component (drag a state, click an edge for its cases, Ctrl + scroll to zoom). The fold-out under it has the NL task, the clauses, the LTLf and the RM text. The expected answer holds all four clauses. Accepted answers 1 and 2 drop the key-before-door precedence the level already forces (answer 1 also the door-before-box one), so they accept the same runs.

# Clauses (all hard, card tpl-response-1-goal, evidence/tpl-response-1-goal.json)

blocks.text: Source: `evidence/judge.out` (chain-regression judge, 2026-11-20 09:47, 100 greedy episodes per run). "Hard rules held" is the judge's success: every hard clause of the card's expected answer holds in the episode. "Goal" is the environment's own success flag. RM return is the mean machine return of the greedy episode.

Per machine: steps to 0.9 eval success `[221184, 241664, 262144]` (expect), `[282624, 303104, 303104]` (ok1), `[262144, 282624, 323584]` (ok2); none "never". The expected machine reaches 0.9 first, the two machines that name no key step (ok1, ok2) take 40k to 60k steps longer; the key alone earns nothing on them, so the start is slower, not blocked.
